definitions.gloss: lucky charm; good-luck item; talisman; auspicious object
definitions.explanation: An object believed to bring good fortune. In Japanese culture, this includes items like daruma dolls, beckoning cats (maneki-neko), and certain foods served at New Year.

examples.japanese: ⟦だるま→だるま：06539_daruma⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{縁起物|えんぎもの}だ。
⟦お{正月|しょうがつ}→お正月：05586_oshougatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{縁起物|えんぎもの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飾|かざ}る→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧⟦{習慣|しゅうかん}→習慣：01429_shuukan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There is a custom of displaying lucky items at New Year.

examples.japanese: ⟦{受験生|じゅけんせい}→受験生：18622_jukensei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{縁起物|えんぎもの}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦お{菓子|かし}→お菓子：02852_okashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦プレゼント→プレゼント：01791_purezento⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I gave the exam student a good-luck candy as a gift.

notes:
USAGE:
Japanese culture has many {縁起物|えんぎもの}, including ⟦{招|まね}き{猫|ねこ}→招き猫：06538_manekineko⟧ (beckoning cat), ⟦だるま→だるま：06539_daruma⟧ (daruma doll), ⟦{熊手|くまで}→熊手：13513_kumade⟧ (bamboo rake — for raking in good fortune), and certain New Year foods. During exam season, snacks with names that sound like "pass" (⟦{勝|か}つ→勝つ：01199_katsu⟧, etc.) are also sold as {縁起物|えんぎもの}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {縁起物|えんぎもの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飾|かざ}る→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧ (to display a lucky charm)
- {縁起物|えんぎもの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{贈|おく}る→贈る：09862_okuru⟧ (to give a good-luck item as a gift)
